policy_title: Implement Cass Review Recommendations on Gender Care
stated: The Conservative Party will complete the implementation of the Cass Review, protecting young people questioning their gender from ideologically-driven care, ensuring NHS services follow evidence-based practices, and legislating to permanently prevent private prescription and supply of puberty blockers.

source.quote: We will complete the implementation of the Cass Review, protecting young people questioning their gender from ideologically-driven care and ensuring that NHS services follow evidence-based best practice. We have already stopped the routine use by the NHS of puberty blockers for gender dysphoria and will legislate to permanently prevent their private prescription and supply.

bearing_set.reason: Directly restructures NHS gender services for minors and legislates to ban private prescription of puberty blockers, materially affecting clinical access and treatment pathways for gender-questioning young people.

Permanent legislative prohibition on private prescription of puberty blockers specifically for gender-questioning youth constitutes a legal restriction on a minority group's access to a medical treatment, raising genuine equal-treatment and bodily-autonomy rights questions.

Legislating to permanently ban private prescription and supply of puberty blockers directly curtails bodily autonomy — state coercion preventing individuals (and parents acting for minors) from accessing treatments even through private means, a clear O10 worsening mechanism.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the clinical/access restructuring lands on O3; the minority-specific restriction raises a real O9 equal-treatment question; and the private-prescription ban is a concrete bodily-autonomy restriction on O10. No material fiscal (O12) or broader prosperity/inequality effect clears the non-negligible bar.
